# Skill Pack

Twenty skills in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and six subagents in `agents/`. The skills
are the process logic of the SDLC pipeline; `tkt` is the adapter shim underneath them.
`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is **always** the canonical version — every other file on disk
is derived from it.

## Portability rules (non-negotiable in skill text)

1. **No backend specifics.** Semantic verbs only — never `acli`, `gh issue`, Jira REST,
   or Linear GraphQL for ticketing.
2. **No repo or toolchain hardcoding.** Repo names, branch formats, reviewers, build
   and test commands, deploy workflows all come from `tkt cfg` lookups.
3. **Roles, not lane names.** `tkt transition KEY review`, never the literal lane.
   `tkt lane review` exists for the rare case you need the provider's string.
4. **Respect `type_class`.** `full_sdlc` runs the full pipeline; `deliverable`
   short-circuits through `complete-deliverable` straight to `done`.
5. **Treat `worklog`/`lane-time` as possibly no-op.** Comments must still read
   naturally when time tracking is off.
6. **Optional verbs are opt-in.** `create`/`apply`/`edit`/`link` may exit 3; branch on
   the code rather than assuming availability.

VCS and infra steps are still GitHub- and cloud-shaped (PRs and CI go through `gh`),
but every value they use comes from config; genuinely infra-specific steps are marked
`PROJECT-SPECIFIC` in the skill text.

## Trust-scoped subagents

`agents/` ships to `.claude/agents/`. The scoping exists so the pipeline can never
self-approve: `sdlc-executor` may read/write files and run build/test but cannot push
or transition; `sdlc-reviewer`, `sdlc-planner`, and `ticket-researcher` are read-only;
`sdlc-verifier` may read and run build/test only; `qa-engineer` may write tests and run
the test runner. Every phase that delegates also states an inline fallback, so harnesses
without subagent support run the pipeline unchanged.

## Harness translation tiers

The `sync-skills` skill defines how the canonical skill is translated:

- **Tier A — every skill:** `.agents/skills/`, `.kiro/skills/`, `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`,
  `.gemini/commands/*.toml`.
- **Tier B — the seven core pipeline skills only** (`select-ticket`, `triage-ticket`,
  `plan-ticket`, `open-pr`, `self-review`, `respond-to-review`, `deploy-ready`):
  `.cursor/`, `.windsurf/`, `.clinerules/`, `.continue/`, `.augment/`,
  `.agents/workflows/`, `.opencode/commands/`.
- **Tier C — rules-style targets, NOT per-skill:** root `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/`,
  `.kiro/steering/`, and friends. Only touch these when project-wide conventions
  change, never because one skill changed.

## Distribution: `tkt sync-pack`

[`sync_pack()`](mex://function:6858d0b0c05a3d7fe774306dcc8fbe71) installs the pack into
a consumer repo as **committed copies**, because cloud harnesses and CI only see
tracked files — the symlinks `tkt init --link-skills` writes are invisible to them.

Its guarantees, all of which are load-bearing:

- Only ever writes paths it records in `.sdlc/pack-manifest.json`. **Never deletes.**
- **Idempotent**: a second run with an unchanged pack makes zero changes on disk,
  including the manifest, so `git status` stays clean.
- Never touches content outside the `AGENTS.md` marker region it manages.
- Runs before config exists — it never calls `Config.load()`.
- Refuses to install into the pack checkout itself (`UsageError`).

**Harness selection is additive and sticky.**
[`_resolve_harnesses()`](mex://function:2ea0c4e9c857a9b390334dd63ce28d66) unions the
harnesses recorded by previous syncs with any newly named ones, so a later bare
`tkt sync-pack` keeps every installed harness current instead of reverting to the
default three (`claude`, `copilot`, `kiro`). `--list-harnesses` prints the registry
and what this project already installs, and writes nothing.

## The managed `AGENTS.md` block

In a consumer repo, `sync-pack` maintains a block delimited by
`<!-- tkt-pack:begin -->` / `<!-- tkt-pack:end -->`.
[`_splice_block()`](mex://function:9b7b64df36b8b36611b5271695239778) preserves
everything outside the markers verbatim, appends the block when markers are absent, and
creates the file when it does not exist.

The block's contents come from
[`_agents_block()`](mex://function:d36dfd25c30c1df2563f78d0367231a2), which lists every
installed skill with a one-liner pulled by
[`_skill_oneliner()`](mex://function:c56b69cb958e6bca40e6b32febe1abee) — the **first
sentence of the skill's frontmatter `description`**. Two consequences worth
internalising:

- Editing a skill's `description` rewrites the managed block in every consumer repo on
  their next sync. It is a public-facing string, not a note to yourself.
- The block must be byte-stable across runs or idempotency breaks, which is why it is
  generated deterministically from the sorted skill set.

`sync-skills` is excluded from what ships — it is a pack-internal meta skill.

This repo's own `AGENTS.md` has **no** managed block and is hand-maintained.

## Staleness reporting

`tkt sync-pack --check` reports missing, locally-modified, and out-of-date pack files
and exits 1. `tkt doctor` folds in
[`doctor_check()`](mex://function:12b5420e646ba6ba58f0ac52a4bc1639), which is only a
non-fatal hint: it returns `None` when there is no manifest, and otherwise an
always-ok `Check` comparing the manifest's `pack_commit` against the pack checkout's
current git HEAD.

`scripts/smoke-sync-pack.sh` is the end-to-end test for all of the above — fresh
install, idempotency, local-modification restore and warning, `--check` exit status,
`--all-harnesses`, `AGENTS.md` custom-content preservation, and named/sticky harness
selection. Run it after any change to `core/pack.py` or the shipped file set.
